Day #1 of recommending “Endling, Extinction Is Forever”. Hello, Kori and fellow commentators/ samurai! This game departs from the horror genre typically featured on your channel; however, it remains thrilling, stressful, and at times, it challenges your thinking. Endling is a mesmerizing indie game that invites players into the poignant journey of a mother fox. Explore a stunningly crafted world where your heart races as you strive to protect your adorable pups. As you navigate through the vibrant but perilous landscape, you'll encounter a myriad of dangers—ruthless hunters, cunning traps, and watchful owls lurking in the shadows. The haunting beauty of nature is juxtaposed with the harsh realities of extreme deforestation, pollution, and the ever-looming specter of starvation. With every step, the bond between mother and pups deepens, making each moment a delicate dance of survival against a world that is both breathtakingly beautiful and chillingly unforgiving. Embrace the challenge and immerse yourself in this evocative tale of resilience and love. In a work so corrupt, you struggle to feed your pups and teach them new skills. This game ranges from $5.00 to $30.00; however, it's an eye-opening game that I can assure you and your viewers will not regret. What do my fellow commentators think?

Content: Cory, can I just say this, I really liked this game and the gameplay you did, cause it reminded me a lot of the kinds of content I miss from you since 2020-2021, especially those horror playthroughs that had a pure or clean vibe, no necessary/unnecessary vulgarity and weirdness. You see, I have been watching you from 2019, since which I had started seeing your videos, and that you were my favorite for a while...I don't know what it is to describe but that one version of you hits different, and honestly, I really miss it sometimes. We are definitely different people, both with their own style and preferences, but I still find myself admiring the way you tell stories or react during gameplay. There is this certain narrative magic you have, even if I don’t always vibe with the tone or direction of every video, I still appreciate it dearly. Matter of fact some of those older videos (not older than 2015) still give me that comforting feeling of nostalgia and contentment or entertainment I cannot forget. But lately, it feels like that feeling has gone into something of an existential crisis. Like something important is fading, and I don't know if it’s me or the content that is changing. I notice how certain aspects that used to make your videos enjoyable for everyone sometimes get left behind. I wish I could message you on Instagram, just once, to tell you what I am going through right now in my life. It isn't about attention, nor for sympathy...just to talk. I really still haven’t found anyone I can truly connect or trust with yet, and sometimes that makes things feel heavier. Still, though I am not sure if you will see this, I want to thank you for those memories, for the laughs, and for the moments when your videos brought light into my day.

Content: I doubt Cory will see this, but I gotta talk about Monsters We Make bro. I preordered it, so I got it quite some time ago, but I didn’t start reading it until today. The reason I didn’t start reading it is because I wanted to wait until I had finished the Berserk deluxe editions that I had, planning to start monsters we make after Volume 4 of Berserk. I finished volume 4 yesterday and woke up feeling sick today. This happened relatively often, as I have pretty bad acid reflux. Normally, when my reflux hits, I take a warm bath because it seems to soothe my stomach. This morning, when I was about to walk to the bathroom to take a nice, warm bath, I spotted out of the corner of my eye, Monsters We Make. Naturally, having finished the berserk deluxe edition volumes I had, I decided it’d be the perfect time to pick up MWM and read the first chapter, so I got into the bath and began reading. I finished the first chapter… and then moved onto the second, then the third, you get the idea. The fact that I went into it saying “yeah I’ll read a chapter” and then just read the ENTIRE first volume in one sitting speaks volumes to me. I had high hopes for MWM, but I didn’t expect it to hook me as easily and as effortlessly as it did. Again, I doubt Cory will see this, but incredible work‼️

 Healthy Sugar-Free Brownies

 Ingredients:

1/2 cup (120g) unsweetened applesauce (natural sweetener substitute)

1/4 cup (60ml) melted coconut oil or unsalted butter

2 large eggs

1 tsp vanilla extract

1/3 cup (40g) cocoa powder (unsweetened)

1/2 cup (60g) almond flour (or oat flour for a softer texture)

1/2 tsp baking powder

Pinch of salt

Optional natural sweetener: 2 tbsp erythritol or stevia (if you need a slightly sweeter taste)

Optional: sugar-free dark chocolate chips or chopped walnuts




 Instructions:

Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Line an 8x8 inch baking dish with parchment paper or lightly grease it.


In a bowl, whisk together the applesauce, eggs, vanilla, and melted coconut oil until smooth.


Sift in the cocoa powder, almond flour, baking powder, and salt. Stir until fully combined.


If desired, fold in sugar-free chocolate chips or nuts.


Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly.


Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out with a few moist crumbs.


Let cool in the pan for 10–15 minutes before slicing. The texture gets fudgier as it cools.

CoryxKenshin – A True Legend of YouTube

In the ever-growing universe of YouTube, where millions create and compete for attention, very few manage to leave behind a legacy. One of those rare, shining stars is CoryxKenshin. With his unique blend of humor, heart, and humility, Cory has become more than just a content creator—he’s a symbol of positivity, resilience, and realness. Over the years, he’s earned the respect of millions around the world and solidified his place as one of the greatest YouTubers of all time.

Cory first began uploading videos in 2009, but it wasn’t until years later that his channel truly exploded in popularity—largely thanks to his playthrough of “Ao Oni”, a Japanese horror RPG. These videos showed off his hilarious reactions, his ability to build suspense, and his unmatched charisma. For many fans, Ao Oni was their introduction to the world of CoryxKenshin, and it still stands as one of his most iconic series. It wasn’t just the gameplay—it was him. The way he made people laugh, jump, and cheer along with him created a connection that went far beyond the screen.

Since then, Cory has taken on some of the scariest and most popular games out there, from Five Nights at Freddy’s to Little Nightmares, Outlast, and Resident Evil. His gameplay series are not just entertaining—they feel like shared adventures with a friend. He even helped push some indie horror games into the spotlight just by playing them, showing how powerful his influence is in the gaming community.

But his achievements go beyond viral videos. In 2021, CoryxKenshin hit a major milestone: 10 million subscribers—a goal he once joked about reaching before “retiring.” While fans feared he might step away for good, his return reminded everyone why he’s so beloved. He now has over 17 million subscribers (and counting), a massive community known as the Samurai, who proudly support him no matter how long he’s away.

Cory has also used his platform for good. He’s raised money for charity, promoted mental health awareness, and spoken openly about his Christian faith, encouraging people to stay true to their values. He’s never been afraid to be himself—even if that meant taking breaks when he needed to protect his mental and emotional well-being. That honesty makes him stand out in an industry where burnout and pressure are too common.

Even YouTube itself has recognized Cory’s impact. In 2022, he was featured in YouTube Rewind-style highlight videos and celebrated by fans across the globe. He’s one of the few creators who can vanish for months and still return to millions of views and love—that’s greatness.

In every way that matters, CoryxKenshin has proven he’s not just another gaming YouTuber. He’s a culture-shaper, a beacon of positivity, and a true icon of the internet. His journey from uploading Ao Oni in a small room to becoming one of the most respected creators on the platform is a story of dedication, faith, and love for his community.

CoryxKenshin isn’t just great. He’s legendary.
